newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker, LME stocks dip expected.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker, LME stocks dip expected.

text.p: COMEX copper settled weaker in heavy volume after profit-taking but much of the week's sharp gains remain largely unthreatened as the market headed for an expected drop in LME stocks on Friday, traders said.
"The uptrend is intact," Fred Demler of E.D. and F. Man International said.

The technical relative strength index (RSI) was about 65 percent, indicating the market still looked overbought and a downward correction may be in the cards, but there was good support at 109.50 to 110.50 cents in the March contract, Demler added.
The LME backwardation weakened to $58/$63, down over $10 since Wednesday.
Most active May COMEX went out 1.30 cents weaker at 111.35 cents per pound, traded 112.65 to 110.90 cents. Spot March settled 0.90 cent off at 113.95 cents.
Volume was heavy at an estimated 22,000 lots with 4,299 switches as the rollover from March to May continued.
Brokers noted good two-way business, and pricing of material by consumers and producers, with producer selling in 1997 and some options-related forward selling in 1998.

ASARCO said earlier this month it had not sold material forward to complete the second leg of a synthetic put operation after buying call options on 149.5 million pounds of copper evenly spread throughout 1997.

With this week's price hike, brokers said ASARCO would almost certainly have sold some metal forward because prices are now above the call option strike prices of $1.04 a lb as far forward as September.
But the total tonnage of ASARCO's operation was seen by some as too small to cap the market.
LME stocks were expected to fall by up to 5,000 tonnes Friday, with some declines in the U.S. due to spot COMEX moving back to a premium over LME cash.
Meanwhile RTZ Corp said on Thursday its 270,000 tonnes per year Kennecott Utah Copper smelter will be running at full capacity by mid-year following a six-week partial shutdown from April.
The smelter was operating at only 51 percent of design capacity by the end of the fourth quarter, the company has said.
In the physical market, traders and producers said demand was still good with premiums firm at just under 3.00 cents per pound over spot COMEX.
On Wednesday May has settled 3.40 cents firmer with open interest rising 1,556 lots to 60,311 lots, indicating fresh buying helped to boost prices rather than just shortcovering.
